gather.answer: Draft answer for 5.1.1, from the evidence found.

requirements.reason: Only recommended methods are allowed, and the encryption check found an old protocol on one server and switched it off.

citations.quote: We use only methods that current national technical guidelines recommend:
Old test web server | TLS 1.0 | Failed; the old protocol was switched off on 24 September and the server passed a rescan

requirements.reason: Methods, key strengths and the key lifecycle are set out, and the encryption check shows disks encrypted and keys renewed within two years.

citations.quote: A key is renewed at least every two years, withdrawn at once when it may have been exposed, and deleted when the data it protects is gone.
The key vault holds 41 keys; none is older than two years, and two were renewed this month.

requirements.reason: The standard says we keep the keys for confidential data that providers process, but nothing shows which providers this applies to.

citations.quote: Where a service provider processes our confidential information, we keep the keys that protect it ourselves, in our key vault, unless the information security officer approves an exception in writing.
